When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
And when the decision had been made that we were to go by sea to Italy, they gave Paul and certain other prisoners into the care of a captain named Julius, of the Augustan band.
非斯都既然定規了，叫我們坐船往意大利去，便將保羅和別的囚犯交給御營裡的一個百夫長，名叫猶流。
We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
And we went to sea in a ship of Adramyttium which was sailing to the sea towns of Asia, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
有一隻亞大米田的船，要沿著亞細亞一帶地方的海邊走，我們就上了那船開行；有馬其頓的帖撒羅尼迦人亞里達古和我們同去。
The next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul with consideration, allowing him to visit his friends and receive their care.
And on the day after, we came to Sidon; and Julius was kind to Paul, and let him go to see his friends and take a rest.
第二天，到了西頓；猶流寬待保羅，准他往朋友那裡去，受他們的照應。
After putting out from there, we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
And sailing again from there, we went on under cover of Cyprus, because the wind was against us.
從那裡又開船，因為風不順，就貼著塞浦路斯背風岸行去。
And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.
And having gone across the sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia we came to Myra, in Lycia.
過了基利家、旁非利亞前面的海，就到了呂家的每拉。
There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.
And there the captain came across a ship of Alexandria, sailing for Italy, and put us in it.
在那裡，百夫長遇見一隻亞歷山大的船，要往意大利去，便叫我們上了那船。
After sailing slowly for many days, we arrived off Cnidus. When the wind impeded us, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
And when we had gone on slowly for a long time, and had had hard work getting across to Cnidus, for the wind was against us, we went under cover of Crete, in the direction of Salmone;
一連多日，船行得慢，僅僅來到革尼土的對面。因為被風攔阻，就貼著克里特背風岸，從撒摩尼對面行過。
After we had moved along the coast with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
And sailing down the side of it, as well as we were able, we came to a certain place named Fair Havens, near which was the town of Lasea.
我們沿岸行走，僅僅來到一個地方，名叫佳澳；離那裡不遠，有拉西亞城。
By now much time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous because it was after the Fast. So Paul advised them,
And as a long time had gone by, and the journey was now full of danger, because it was late in the year, Paul put the position before them,
走的日子多了，已經過了禁食的節期，行船又危險，保羅就勸眾人說：
“Men, I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss, not only to ship and cargo, but to our own lives as well.”
Saying, Friends, I see that this journey will be one of great damage and loss, not only to the goods and the ship, but to ourselves.
「眾位，我看這次行船，不但貨物和船要受傷損，大遭破壞，連我們的性命也難保。」
But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.
But the captain gave more attention to the master and the owner of the ship than to what Paul said.
但百夫長信從掌船的和船主，不信從保羅所說的。
Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, if somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.

And as the harbour was not a good one in which to be for the winter, the greater number of them were for going out to sea, in order, if possible, to put in for the winter at Phoenix, a harbour of Crete, looking to the north-east and south-east.
且因在這海口過冬不便，船上的人就多半說，不如開船離開這地方，或者能到菲尼基過冬。菲尼基是克里特的一個海口，一面朝東北，一面朝東南。
When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.
And when the south wind came softly, being of the opinion that their purpose might be effected, they let the ship go and went sailing down the side of Crete, very near to the land.
這時，微微起了南風，他們以為得意，就起了錨，貼近克里特行去。
But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.
But after a little time, a very violent wind, named Euraquilo, came down from it with great force.
不多幾時，狂風從島上撲下來；那風名叫「友拉革羅」。
Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.
And when the ship got into the grip of it, and was not able to make headway into the wind, we gave way, and went before it.
船被風抓住，敵不住風，我們就任風颳去。
Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.
And, sailing near the side of a small island named Cauda, we were able, though it was hard work, to make the ship's boat safe:
貼著一個小島的背風岸奔行，那島名叫高大，在那裡僅僅收住了小船。
After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.
And having got it up, they put cords under and round the ship; but fearing that they might be pushed on to the Syrtis, they let down the sails and so went running before the wind.
既然把小船拉上來，就用纜索捆綁船底，又恐怕在賽耳底沙灘上擱了淺，就落下篷來，任船飄去。
We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.
And, still fighting the storm with all our strength, the day after they made a start at getting the goods out of the ship;
我們被風浪逼得甚急，第二天眾人就把貨物拋在海裡。
On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
And on the third day, they let all the sailing apparatus go over the side.
到第三天，他們又親手把船上的器具拋棄了。
When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.
And as we had not seen the sun or stars for a long time, and a great storm was on us, all hope of salvation was gone.
太陽和星辰多日不顯露，又有狂風大浪催逼，我們得救的指望就都絕了。

After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.

And when they had been without food for a long time, Paul got up among them and said, Friends, it would have been better if you had given attention to me and not gone sailing out from Crete, to undergo this damage and loss.
眾人多日沒有吃甚麼，保羅就出來站在他們中間，說：「眾位，你們本該聽我的話，不離開克里特，免得遭這樣的傷損破壞。
But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.
But now, I say to you, be of good heart, for there will be no loss of life, but only of the ship.
現在我還勸你們放心，你們的性命一個也不失喪，惟獨失喪這船。
For just last night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me
For this night there came to my side an angel of the God who is my Master and whose servant I am,
因我所屬所事奉的神，他的使者昨夜站在我旁邊，說：
and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’
Saying, Have no fear, Paul, for you will come before Caesar, and God has given to you all those who are sailing with you.
『保羅，不要害怕，你必定站在凱撒面前，並且與你同船的人，神都賜給你了。』
So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.
And so, O men, be of good heart, for I have faith in God that it will be as he said to me.
所以眾位可以放心，我信神他怎樣對我說，事情也要怎樣成就。
However, we must run aground on some island.”
But we will be sent on to a certain island.
只是我們必要撞在一個島上。」
On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
But when the fourteenth day came, while we were going here and there in the Adriatic sea, about the middle of the night the sailors had an idea that they were getting near land;
到了第十四天夜間，船在亞得里亞海飄來飄去。約到半夜，水手以為漸近旱地，
They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.
And they let down the lead, and saw that the sea was a hundred and twenty feet deep; and after a little time they did it again and it was ninety feet.
就探深淺，探得有十二丈；稍往前行，又探深淺，探得有九丈。
Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.
Then, fearing that by chance we might come on to the rocks, they let down four hooks from the back of the ship, and made prayers for the coming of day.
恐怕撞在石頭上，就從船尾拋下四個錨，盼望天亮。
Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.
Then the sailors made attempts secretly to get away from the ship, letting down a boat as if they were about to put down hooks from the front of the ship;
水手想要逃出船去，把小船放在海裡，假作要從船頭拋錨的樣子。
But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”
But Paul said to the captain and his men, If you do not keep these men in the ship, you will not be safe.
保羅對百夫長和兵丁說：「這些人若不等在船上，你們必不能得救。」
So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.
Then the armed men, cutting the cords of the boat, let her go.
於是兵丁砍斷小船的繩子，由它飄去。
Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.
And when dawn was near, Paul gave them all orders to take food, saying, This is the fourteenth day you have been waiting and taking no food.
天漸亮的時候，保羅勸眾人都吃飯，說：「你們懸望忍餓不吃甚麼，已經十四天了。
So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”
So I make request to you to take food; for this is for your salvation: not a hair from the head of any of you will come to destruction.
所以我勸你們吃飯，這是關乎你們救命的事；因為你們各人連一根頭髮也不至於損壞。」
After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
And when he had said this and had taken bread, he gave praise to God before them all, and took a meal of the broken bread.
保羅說了這話，就拿著餅，在眾人面前祝謝了神，擘開吃。
They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.
Then they all took heart and did the same.
於是他們都放下心，也就吃了。
In all, there were 276 of us on board.
And we were, in the ship, two hundred and seventy-six persons.
我們在船上的共有二百七十六個人。
After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
And when they had had enough food, they made the weight of the ship less, turning the grain out into the sea.
他們吃飽了，就把船上的麥子拋在海裡，為要叫船輕一點。
When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.
And when it was day, they had no knowledge of the land, but they saw an inlet of the sea with a floor of sand, and they had the idea of driving the ship up on to it if possible.
「到了天亮，他們不認識那地方，但見一個海灣，有岸可登，就商議能把船攏進去不能。
Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
So cutting away the hooks, and letting them go into the sea, and freeing the cords of the guiding-blades, and lifting up the sail to the wind, they went in the direction of the inlet.
於是砍斷纜索，棄錨在海裡；同時也鬆開舵繩，拉起頭篷，順著風向岸行去。
But the vessel struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.
And coming to a point between two seas, they got the ship to land; and the front part was fixed in the sand and not able to be moved, but the back part was broken by the force of the waves.
但遇著兩水夾流的地方，就把船擱了淺；船頭膠住不動，船尾被浪的猛力衝壞。
The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.
Then the armed men were for putting the prisoners to death, so that no one would get away by swimming.
兵丁的意思要把囚犯殺了，恐怕有洑水脫逃的。
But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
But the captain, desiring to keep Paul safe, kept them from their purpose, and gave orders that those who had knowledge of swimming were to go off the ship and get first to land:
但百夫長要救保羅，不准他們任意而行，就吩咐會洑水的，跳下水去先上岸；
The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.
And the rest, some on boards and some on things from the ship. And so it came about that they all got safe to land.
其餘的人可以用板子或船上的零碎東西上岸。這樣，眾人都得了救，上了岸。
